name: AR/VR & Spatial Computing
tagline: Create immersive 3D experiences for headsets, smart glasses and phones.

overview.summary: AR (augmented reality) places digital content on top of the real world — through phone cameras or smart glasses. VR (virtual reality) puts users inside a fully digital world through a headset. 'Spatial computing' is the umbrella term for apps that understand 3D space, hands, eyes and voice. Developers in this field build training simulations, games, product visualisers, medical and architecture tools, and increasingly AI-powered assistants on smart glasses. The core skills are real-time 3D development (Unity, Unreal), 3D maths and interaction design.
whyTrending: Big platforms are competing on spatial devices: Apple Vision Pro (visionOS), Meta Quest headsets and Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, and Google's Android XR platform with Samsung's Galaxy XR headset (launched October 2025).
AI assistants on camera-equipped smart glasses are a new product category that needs developers who combine computer vision, AI and spatial UX.
Enterprises use XR for training, remote assistance and digital twins in manufacturing, healthcare and construction, which is steadier than consumer gaming demand.
The skills transfer well: Unity and Unreal developers can move between games, XR, simulation and digital-twin work — useful protection in a still-maturing market.

roles.title: XR / Unity Developer
roles.description: Builds AR/VR apps and games in Unity with C#, handling interaction, physics and performance on headsets.

roles.title: Unreal Engine Developer
roles.description: Creates high-fidelity XR, simulation and visualisation experiences in Unreal with C++ and Blueprints.

roles.title: visionOS / Spatial App Developer
roles.description: Builds apps for Apple Vision Pro with Swift, SwiftUI and RealityKit.

roles.title: WebXR Developer
roles.description: Builds browser-based AR/VR experiences with Three.js, Babylon.js or A-Frame — no app install required.

roles.title: 3D Technical Artist
roles.description: Bridges art and code: optimises 3D models, shaders, lighting and pipelines for real-time performance.

roles.title: XR Interaction / UX Designer
roles.description: Designs comfortable, intuitive spatial interactions — hand tracking, gaze, menus and onboarding.

beginner: C# (for Unity) or C++ basics (for Unreal)
Unity or Unreal editor basics: scenes, objects, components
3D fundamentals: coordinates, transforms, meshes, materials, lighting
Vector maths: positions, directions, dot and cross products
Git (with Git LFS for large assets)
intermediate: AR Foundation (ARKit/ARCore): plane detection, anchors, image tracking
Performance profiling: frame rate, draw calls, LOD
advanced: Shaders and rendering optimisation for mobile/standalone headsets
Computer vision and AI integration (object recognition, scene understanding)
Spatial UX: comfort, accessibility and motion-sickness prevention

stack.note: Unity + C# appears in the majority of XR listings; Unreal is common for high-end simulation and automotive/architecture visualisation.

roadmap.title: 3D and engine basics
goals: Install Unity (free Personal licence) and finish the Unity Essentials pathway
Learn C# basics through small scripts
Understand transforms, cameras, lighting and materials
Learn basic Blender to make and export simple models
roadmap.milestone: A small playable 3D scene with your own scripts and assets.

roadmap.title: AR and VR fundamentals
goals: Build a phone AR app with AR Foundation (place objects on surfaces)
Set up the XR Interaction Toolkit and build a VR room with grab interactions
Test in the XR Device Simulator if you don't have a headset
Add UI panels and comfortable locomotion
Profile performance and hit target frame rates
roadmap.milestone: One AR phone app and one VR prototype, each with a demo video.

roadmap.title: Polish and specialise
goals: Build a WebXR demo with Three.js that anyone can try in a browser
Add an AI feature (e.g. voice commands or object recognition)
Learn spatial UX guidelines from Apple, Meta and Google
Publish a demo on itch.io, the Meta Horizon store (App Lab successor) or the web
Join an XR game jam or hackathon
roadmap.milestone: A polished portfolio with three XR projects and published demos.

interview.question: AR vs VR vs MR?
interview.answer: AR overlays digital content on the real world; VR replaces the world with a digital one; MR (mixed reality) blends both so digital objects interact with the real environment.

interview.question: Why is frame rate so important in VR?
interview.answer: Low or unstable frame rates and latency cause discomfort and motion sickness. Standalone headsets typically target 72–90+ FPS, so every millisecond of frame time matters.

interview.question: What is OpenXR?
interview.answer: A royalty-free standard from Khronos that lets XR apps run across many headsets and platforms with one API.

interview.question: How does AR plane detection work?
interview.answer: The device tracks visual feature points and motion (visual-inertial odometry) to estimate its pose and detect flat surfaces where content can be anchored.

interview.question: How do you reduce draw calls?
interview.answer: Batch static objects, use texture atlases, share materials, use GPU instancing, LODs and occlusion culling.

interview.question: What causes motion sickness in VR and how do you avoid it?
interview.answer: Mismatch between visual motion and the inner ear. Use teleport or snap-turn options, avoid forced camera movement, keep a stable horizon and high frame rates.

interview.question: Explain the dot product in a game/XR context.
interview.answer: It measures how aligned two vectors are — e.g. checking if an object is in front of the user or how directly they're looking at a target.

interview.question: What is a quaternion and why use it?
interview.answer: A four-number representation of rotation that avoids gimbal lock and interpolates smoothly, so engines use it internally for orientation.

interview.question: How do you design UI for spatial apps?
interview.answer: Place UI at comfortable distance and angles, use large targets, support hands/gaze/controllers, keep text legible, and avoid locking UI rigidly to the head.

interview.question: How would you test an XR app without a headset?
interview.answer: Use device simulators (XR Device Simulator, visionOS simulator, Android XR emulator), then validate on real hardware before release because comfort and performance differ.

demandNotes.bangladesh: Small but present: game studios and agencies build AR/VR for foreign clients, education and marketing. Unity skills open the most doors.
demandNotes.remote: Moderate. Enterprise training, simulation and AR marketing projects hire remote Unity developers.
demandNotes.global: Growing but uneven — strong in enterprise training, defence/simulation and smart glasses; consumer VR is more volatile.

startToday: Install Unity Hub and the latest Unity LTS version
Start the free Unity Essentials pathway on Unity Learn
Try a WebXR demo on threejs.org with your phone
Download Blender and follow a beginner 'donut' or low-poly tutorial
Check whether your phone supports ARCore or ARKit
Pick one real-world problem an AR or VR app could solve
